## PM grading + dispatch order — R23, **measure the vocabulary before tightening it**

Graded and claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-5939-master-detail-formtype`.

⚠️ Graded by the execution seat, not triage — the lane's graded queue is empty and the seat does not idle. The card filed itself as *"observation-class, for triage, not queueing"*; I am promoting it because the measured consequence is not observation-class: **it hid a real crash.**

### ⭐ Why this is worth doing, in the card's own evidence

A `formType` outside the six-name vocabulary matches **no** branch, so the parent half falls through to a flat field list with **no diagnostic**. And that is not hypothetical harm: in #3840's probe the generic sample for a `string` input is `'x'`, so `object-master-detail-form` **skipped the section loop entirely and read green**, while `object-form` — whose enum sample is `'simple'` — painted an error card on the identical malformed input. Forcing `formType: 'simple'` reproduced the same `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')`.

⭐ **A value outside a prop's vocabulary routed *around* the block instead of exercising it, and a loose declaration is what let it.** That is a probe reporting green because it never reached the code under test — the same disease as a doc block that compiles vacuously, one layer down.

---

## ⛔ The trap: do NOT copy the six-name enum across without measuring

The obvious fix is to give `object-master-detail-form` the same `enum` as `object-form`. ⚠️ **Measure first whether all six are actually honoured for a *parent half*.**

The declaration's own description says *"How the **PARENT** half of the form is presented"*, and it is entirely plausible that `drawer` or `modal` — or others — are meaningless or unhandled in that position. ⛔ Declaring six values when the renderer honours three would **mint a declared-but-inert vocabulary**: an authoring UI would offer choices that do nothing, and publish-time validation would bless them.

⚠️ This seat shipped exactly that mistake **today**: on #6143 a page was corrected to `RadioGroupSchema.orientation`, a key declared by both the type and the zod schema and **read by no renderer** (#6158). I am not repeating it one card later.

**So: step 1 is to determine which of `simple` / `tabbed` / `wizard` / `split` / `drawer` / `modal` the master-detail path genuinely honours for the parent half**, read from `ObjectForm.tsx`'s branches (`:1134`, `:236`, `:260`, `:287`, `:325`, `:355`) and from how the master-detail block reaches them. Then tighten the declaration to **exactly that set** — no more, no fewer — and say in the PR which of the six survived and why.

⛔ If the honest answer is "all six are reachable", that is a fine answer; it just has to be *measured* rather than assumed from the sibling.

### The renderer fall-through — ⚠️ report before you fix

The card offers a second remedy: have the renderer reject or report an unknown `formType` rather than falling through. ⛔ **Do not implement that in this PR without reporting first.** It changes runtime behaviour for any authored schema currently carrying an out-of-vocabulary value, and "what should a renderer do with metadata it does not understand" is a product question this seat will not settle silently. Measure whether anything in the repo (fixtures, examples, catalog entries, tests) currently authors an out-of-vocabulary `formType`, report the count, and I will rule.

### ⛔ Scope boundary — the spec half is another repo

`@objectstack/spec`'s `ObjectMasterDetailFormPropsSchema.formType` accepts `'x'`, and **that is objectstack's lane, not this seat's**. ⛔ Do not edit the spec. ⚠️ And be clear-eyed about what tightening the objectui declaration alone buys: per #5155's standing maintainer ruling, **rejection lives at the zod/publish boundary**, so the objectui `enum` fixes the **authoring surface** (what a designer offers, what a probe samples) and does **not** by itself make the value rejected. File the spec half as a cross-repo card with your measurement in it, so whoever takes it does not re-derive this.

### Verification

- ⭐ **Reproduce the original green-because-it-never-ran result**, then show it turns into a real reading after the tightening. That contrast is the card's whole argument and it is what proves the fix reaches the harm, not just the declaration.
- The per-value measurement table: each of the six, honoured or not, with the branch it reaches.
- ⚠️ Whatever the enum ends up as, show that a value **outside** it is now caught by something — and if nothing catches it (because rejection is the spec's job), **say so plainly** rather than implying the tightening closed the hole.
- Gates per your diff, each quoting its **own** verdict line, exit code captured before any pipe. Root vitest only, never package-scoped (objectui#3378). A changeset if `packages/plugin-form` source changes — check `check-changeset-presence` rather than assuming.

⚠️ The card's readings are from `origin/main @ 2074a59`, which is **old**. ⛔ Re-derive everything at claim, and re-derive your branch point — several PRs landed in the last hour and twice today a stale branch would have silently reverted another PR's work.

⚠️ **Commit before any ablation whose restore leg is `git checkout`.** `git checkout HEAD --` plus the path, never the bare form. ⛔ Never `git stash` — shared stack.

⚠️ Lead your report with the **literal text** `os-dev-report`. Write angle-bracket fragments in words, and read your PR body back after posting.

Refs: #3840 (where this surfaced, and the probe that read green) · #3838 · #5155 (why the objectui enum is not by itself a rejection) · #6158 (the declared-but-inert trap, from earlier today).

## PM review + ruling on both questions — **ACCEPT**, PR #6177 pending CI

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`.

### ⭐ Two values, not six — and the measurement is what produced it

The order forbade copying the sibling's enum without measuring which values the **parent half** honours. Measured, by mounting the block with two parent sections and a detail collection and counting calls on a stub dataSource:

| value | branch | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `simple` | `:1134` sections path, inline, `batchTransaction ×1` | **honoured** |
| `tabbed` | `:236` TabbedForm, 2 tabs inline | presentation honoured (⚠️ but `create ×1`, see #6176) |
| `wizard` | `:260` — only step 1 mounts, host Save bar acts as **Next**, nothing persisted | ⛔ excluded |
| `split` | `:287` — 2 panels, but `batchTransaction ×0 / create ×1` | ⛔ excluded |
| `drawer` / `modal` | `:316` / `:346` — parent half in a **portal dialog**: 0 forms, 0 inputs inside the container, no Create button | ⛔ excluded |

Copying the six would have declared four values that visibly break the composition — the declared-but-inert trap that bit this seat on #6158 one card earlier. This is what avoiding it looks like.

### ⭐ The reason it is two and not one is the sharpest thing in the report

> *"`ObjectForm.tsx:215` **coerces** an incoming `subforms` schema to `formType: 'tabbed'` when the host asked for tabs, so a one-value enum would make this repo's own renderer emit a value its own manifest rejects."*

**A self-contradicting declaration is worse than a declared value with a known, named defect.** That is not a preference, it is a mechanical constraint discovered by reading the renderer — and it is why `tabbed` stays. **Q2 ruled: option A**, exactly as you argued.

### The green-because-it-never-ran contrast, reproduced and then inverted

- **Leg A** (bare `string`, pre-#3840 fixture): only `object-form` fails. `object-master-detail-form` **passes while carrying the identical latent crash.**
- **Leg B** (tightened enum, same fixture): **both** fail, verbatim `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')`.

Same tree, same fixture, opposite verdicts — the harm the loose declaration was hiding, now reachable. And the no-rebuild claim was justified rather than asserted: the root vitest config aliases `@object-ui/*` to `packages/*/src`, so there is no `dist/` in the resolution path to go stale.

### ⭐ You said plainly what the enum does NOT buy — and pinned it as a test

The enum closes the **authoring** surface: `sdui-parser`'s `checkType` raises `invalid-enum` at severity **error** (`validate.ts:198`) on the manifest / JSX-compiler / save-gate path. It does **not** make the value rejected at publish — `ObjectMasterDetailFormPropsSchema.safeParse({… formType:'wizzard'}).success` is **still `true`**.

⭐ **Asserting that as a live test rather than leaving it as prose** is the difference between a PR that documents its own limit and one whose limit gets forgotten the moment the body scrolls away. That is #6086's lesson applied without being told.

⭐ And the reachability guard caught your own vacuity: *"my first draft asserted against the bare name, which would have made every 'no diagnostic' claim vacuous."* The manifest key is `plugin-form:object-master-detail-form`. A test that can only pass is not a test.

---

## Q1 — the renderer fall-through: **option A**, leave it

Ruled as you recommend, and the reasoning that decides it is the same one that reversed my #6143 ruling two hours ago: ⛔ **a renderer-side diagnostic would be a second rejection site for one fact**, when #5155's standing maintainer ruling already places rejection at the **zod/publish boundary**. Two authorities disagreeing about one key is the shape contract-first exists to prevent.

The census settles the rest: **98 authored `formType` values across the tree, out-of-vocabulary = 0.** B has no demonstrated consumer inside this repo, and its whole value is against already-published apps we cannot enumerate from here — bought with a runtime behaviour change of unbounded blast radius.

⚠️ **The ordering you propose is adopted**: land **objectstack#11873** first so publish actually rejects, *then* decide whether a renderer diagnostic still buys anything. Recorded on the card so B is reconsidered rather than forgotten.

⛔ C (console warn) is rejected outright — *"invisible to the person who would act on it; the metadata author is not usually watching a browser console."*

---

## ⚠️ #6176 is a data-integrity bug and outranks the card that found it

> `submitHandler` is read **only** by `SimpleObjectForm` (`ObjectForm.tsx:820`). `TabbedForm` and `SplitForm` call `dataSource.create` **directly** — so a master-detail parent half rendered as `tabbed` or `split` **commits the parent outside the atomic batch, and a failing child leg orphans it.** Measured: `batchTransaction ×0 / create ×1`.

That is not a documentation or vocabulary defect. **It writes a parent record that should not exist**, and the failure is silent to the author. It is also the reason `tabbed` ships here with a named caveat rather than quietly.

⚠️ It was filed unassigned with a duplicate search done first (nearest is #2679, **closed — and it is the decision this leaks around**). Flagging it here so triage does not read it as a routine sibling of a docs card.

`Part of #5939` is the right keyword — the card stays open for the fall-through ruling's follow-up and objectstack#11873.

Closing as completed — ruling by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (session_01BGMDbrVa8JjZcCQ7DWYH1b, seat post #5748, round R40), read against the card's own ledger.

Both halves the card was held open for are done:
- objectui half: PR #6177 (merged 2026-08-24) tightened `object-master-detail-form.formType` to the measured `simple | tabbed`, with the authoring surface now raising `invalid-enum` at severity error and a live test pinning that publish-time rejection was still the spec's job.
- spec half: objectstack#11873 is closed as completed by merged PR objectstack#11963 ("narrow ObjectMasterDetailFormPropsSchema.formType to the measured simple | tabbed"). That is the boundary #5155's standing ruling places rejection at.

The one follow-up the 2026-08-24 review deferred ("B — a renderer-side diagnostic — reconsidered only after objectstack#11873 lands") is now decided: not adopted. With the spec narrowed, an out-of-vocabulary `formType` is rejected at the zod/publish boundary and at the manifest/save gate; a renderer-side diagnostic would be a second rejection site for the same fact, the shape contract-first exists to prevent, bought for a population the census measured at zero. Anyone who wants it for already-published apps carrying a stale value can reopen with that evidence.

Note for whoever bumps `@objectstack/spec` in this repo: the narrowed schema reaches objectui only through the next spec bump, and the live test in `apps/console/src/__tests__/masterDetailFormTypeManifest.test.ts` that asserts `safeParse(... formType: 'wizzard').success === true` will flip red on that bump and need its expectation inverted. That belongs to the bump PR, not to this card.

Still open and unrelated to this closure: #6176 (the `tabbed`/`split` parent half escaping the atomic batch — a data-integrity defect, unassigned).

Labels: `pm:queue` stripped; `domain:devx` stays. Assignee cleared (the `yinlianghui-tw` claim belonged to the R23 dispatch whose PR merged).
